newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Forex controls seen dampening Zimbabwe stocks.
newsitem.headline: Forex controls seen dampening Zimbabwe stocks.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares soared to new record highs in active trade on Wednesday but brokers said a reintroduction of foreign exchange controls on dual-listed stocks could dampen the local bourse's bullishness.
The key 58-counter industrial index leapt 70.31 points to an new all time peak of 10,868.94.

Brokers said the central bank's announcement that the transfer of shares from offshore registers to Zimbabwean registers would now require exchange control approval had had no immediate impact on the market but said it was retrogressive.
"The market considers the measure to retrogressive in terms of liberalisation policies," one broker said.

The central bank had lifted the controls on dual-listed stocks in January but on Wednesday said in a statement it had become necessary for exchange control to look at all cases involving the transfer of shares from foreign to local registers. It did not elaborate.
"The market has been quite bullish but this measure could put a dampener on it," a broker said.

The brokers said counters which would be most affected by the measure included hotel and supermarket group Meikles, merchant banker NMB and southern African conglomerate Trans Zambezi Industries (TZI).
The first two are also quoted on the London exchange while TZI is listed in Luxembourg and Lusaka.
On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Wednesday, Meikles jumped 100 cents to 2,900 as did clothing retailer Truworths to 1,000 while merchant banker FMB soared 200 cents to 5,000.

Sugar producer Hippo rose 40 cents to 1,600, winery Afdis gained 30 cents to 500, TZI and finance group Finhold added 20 cents each to 1,070 and 700 respectively and hotel chain Zimsun put on 15 cents to 400.
A couple of counters bucked the trend, notably pharmaceutical group Caps which dropped 100 cents to 1,800 and Alloys which shed 25 cents to 525.
Minings were quiet and softer with gold investor Falgold edging two cents up to 70 while Wankie Colliery lost 40 cents to 530.
The seven-counter mining index shed 13.55 points to 1,014.15.
